About ELM Construction

ABOUT US

ELM Construction LLC fuses exceptional design with a proven process to meet the remodeling needs of our clients. Founded in 2008, by Elliott Pike, ELM Construction prospered during the worst economic downturn since the Great Depression. Our personal resilience is only a part of our success story: we have grown due to referrals and repeat business from our loyal customers in the community.

HIGHLIGHTS
• 2023 NAHB Remodeler of the Year
• 2026 Chair, NAHB Remodelers

Elliott Pike, the 2023 NAHB Remodeler of the Year, founded ELM Construction, LLC in 2008 as a residential design and remodeling company serving the Birmingham, Ala., area. Under his leadership, ELM has grown steadily and profitably, thanks to his thoughtful approach to building a strong, skilled team.

Over The Mountain Remodeling Firm & Custom Home Builder

As a design/build company based in Homewood, Alabama, we provide remodeling services for Hoover, Homewood, Mountain Brook, and the Birmingham Metro area. Our projects include, but are not limited to, total kitchen remodels, bathroom renovations, basements, outdoor living areas, restoration work (including fire restoration), additions, and whole-home renovations. Regardless of your project’s size, we are with you during every phase, through its completion. We have developed collaborative relationships with skilled tradesmen and knowledgeable suppliers. 

We back our commitment to excellence with a written warranty that covers you for two years—double the industry standard. One way we prove our dedication to the constant improvement of our practices is through various professional credentials. We are licensed by the State of Alabama as a Residential Home Builder / Remodeler and fully insured, with both General Liability Insurance and Workers Compensation. 

We are active in our local, state, and national home building associations and have been recognized for our quality work by several of our industry’s top organizations.

Your Design/Build Remodeling Firm in Homewood, AL

At ELM Construction, our team is built on experience, craftsmanship, and a commitment to getting the job done right. We work together to navigate challenges, find creative solutions, and ensure every project runs smoothly from start to finish.

OUR TEAM

Elliott Pike

FOUNDER

Elliott and his wife, LeArden, started ELM Construction LLC in 2008, Today Elliott oversees the day to day operations. Elliott graduated from Homewood High School and Troy University with a degree in journalism. Before working at ELM Construction, he worked for a company that specialized in remodeling apartment complexes. Prior to that, he worked for a national building materials distributor. Outside of work, Elliott enjoys spending time with his family and friends, working in his yard and traveling.

Adam Martz

PRODUCTION MANAGER / LEAD ESTIMATOR

Adam started at ELM Construction LLC in 2011 as a Project Manager. Today Adam oversees estimating and production. He graduated from Pleasant Grove High School, Bessemer State Technical College with a degree in Building Construction and UAB with a degree in Business Management! Adam grew up working with his family in residential new construction. He enjoys spending time with his family and friends, running/weight training and woodworking.

Liz Kennedy

DESIGNER

Liz joined ELM Construction LLC as a Designer in May of 2020. She went to Thompson High School and attended the University of North Alabama where she obtained her degree in Interior Design. In 2022 she also earned the certification of Certified Kitchen and Bath Designer (CKBD) thru NKBA. Liz lives in Helena with her husband, Michael and three children. In her spare time Liz enjoys religious studies, spending time with her family and retail therapy.

Erin Leist

DESIGNER

Erin joined the ELM team in the Spring of 2024 as our newest designer. Originally from Laurel, Mississippi, she has spent the past few years in Birmingham earning a degree in Interior Design from Samford University, where she is now a recent graduate. Erin grew up always having a passion for design and creative problem-solving spaces. On the weekends, Erin enjoys antique shopping and exploring new places in Birmingham.

Carl Rouss

PROJECT MANAGER

Carl joined the ELM team in 2024 as Project Manager. After attending The University of Montevallo, Carl went to work for a Birmingham-based company with various multi-family projects across the Southeast. In 2021, Carl began managing local custom home projects. There, he gained invaluable experience, working closely with homeowners, subcontractors, and vendors throughout the building process. In his free time, he enjoys songwriting , producing music, and traveling with his family.

Matt Martz

LEAD CARPENTER

Matt has been with ELM Construction LLC since 2014. He graduated from Pleasant Grove High School then attended Lawson State Community College where he earned an associates degree in Commercial Art and Graphic Design. Matt has over 25 years of experience in residential construction and when away from work, he enjoys spending time with his wife Cary, two sons Alec and Landon, and dog Max.

Zolen Boogaerts

PROJECT MANAGER

Zolen joined the ELM team in May of 2024, originally as a carpenter, then moving to Project Manager. He graduated from Vestavia Hills High School, then studied Biology and Spanish at the University of Alabama. While working for a local Birmingham outdoor company, Zolen managed their woodshop building custom store fixtures, cabinets, and also building out new stores. Zolen and his wife moved to Seattle in 2017, where he spent 7 years doing residential remodeling as a carpenter, project manager, and field trainer. After having two children, he and his wife decided to return home to Alabama in 2024, and joined the ELM team. Zolen loves the outdoors and enjoys backpacking, rock climbing, and mountaineering with his family.

ELM Construction’s Design/Build Approach

At ELM Construction, we believe that a successful remodel starts with clear expectations. That’s why we’re sharing our process—so you know what to expect at every stage, from the initial consultation to the final walkthrough. Transparency helps ensure a smoother, more enjoyable experience, giving you confidence in every decision along the way.

OUR PROCESS

Our Simple, 4-Step Process

As a design-build contractor, we streamline the remodeling process by handling both design and construction under one roof. This approach improves coordination, enhances efficiency, and creates more practical, buildable designs—saving you both time and money.

One team, one plan, one contract. That means a seamless experience from the initial concept through construction to project completion.

1

Step 1: Let’s Talk

We see beyond the ordinary to create extraordinary lower-level spaces that extend your living area in meaningful ways. Transform your basement into an entertainment zone with professional acoustics, or create a climate-controlled wine cellar for your collection. A private fitness studio or executive home office can give you the space you need to pursue your passions, while a fully appointed guest suite welcomes visitors in style.

2

Step 2: Let’s Meet

This is our “discovery” meeting and it usually takes one to two hours. Here are some things you should know about this meeting:

We’ll take a tour of your space and encourage you to share your vision for the project. What do you like about the existing space? What do you dislike? What are your needs? Or just as important, what are your wants?

We’ll have a real conversation about what things cost and timelines. It’s important that we all have similar expectations as we move forward.

We encourage everyone that will have ANY input on your project to participate in this meeting. We’ll cover a lot of important information and we want to make sure everyone has an opportunity to ask questions.

>>

Step 3: Let’s Design & Plan

The “project development” phase is perhaps the most important part of the entire process! There are two major components to the “project development” phase; Design and Detail.

DESIGN

We’ll measure the existing spaces to accurately recreate them in our design software, Chief Architect. We can then create conceptual designs for your renovation and review them in our office. We’ll start with drafts of proposed floorplans, elevations, and even 3D renderings of your renovation. Then we'll narrow down the designs to your favorite and start the “details” phase.

DETAILS

Collaborating with our award-winning designer, you’ll begin the selection process. For some, this is the most intimidating part of a renovation. But our designer will shepherd you through the entire process, helping as much or as little as you’d like.

Our experienced team will meet with trade partners at your home to check your existing systems (electrical, plumbing, structural, etc.) and work with the appropriate building departments to make sure your project is feasible. This eliminates or lessens the chance of running into major surprises during the construction process.

At the end of the “project development” phase, we’ll present to you a contract with a detailed scope of work and a guaranteed fixed price!

3

Step 4: Let’s Renovate

Believe it or not, the construction phase is usually the easiest of all phases! You’ve already done most of the hard decision making during the project development phase. Now we finalize the construction schedule, apply for necessary building permits, confirm time tables with our trade partners and start work!

4

Expert Budgeting Guide for Remodeling Costs

At ELM Construction, we specialize in creating spaces that reflect your lifestyle and enhance the functionality of your home. From kitchens and bathrooms to basements, additions, and outdoor living areas, we’re your trusted partner for all your remodeling needs.

BUDGETING

How Much Will My Remodeling Project Cost?

Unfortunately, it’s not as easy as saying “X dollars per square foot.” Unlike new construction, a remodeling project often involves demolition, moving walls, relocating electrical, air conditioning, plumbing, and matching existing finishes.

Without tearing into walls, floors, and ceilings, we can’t be certain what is involved, but, of course, that is not an option before delivering an estimate. We can, however, rely on experience to help identify potential challenges ahead of time and help you plan for the unexpected.

We also consult with you on the specifics of your project, including square footage, the age of your home, location, and a number of other factors to help determine if the budget you’ve set is realistic or if the project needs to be adjusted.

Recognizing this does not fully answer the question, we have provided some realistic examples below to help you have a starting point.

Jump to Pricing Examples
What Contributes to the Cost of a Remodel?

Remodeling projects come in all shapes and sizes and with all types of trim levels. For example, do you want to give your small galley style kitchen a “facelift” or do you want to “gut” and remodel your kitchen, tear down walls and open up the space completely? Do you want to use builder-grade cultured marble in your bathroom or something a little more exotic like  White marble for your countertops?  Following our tried-and-true process, we’ll help you navigate these questions so our cost estimator can give you an exact guaranteed cost you can expect to pay for your project!

Can You Give Me a Ballpark Price for My  Remodel?

Sure! Below you will find a list of different types of projects with typical home renovation cost ranges.  Please keep in mind that every project is unique and prices will vary (and may even end up costing more or less than the price ranges shown).  Our goal by sharing this information is to help you make an informed and educated decision about your project. 

The remodeling cost information we provide assumes we will provide you with a complete construction project from permitting and construction through final inspection and cleaning.  It includes all labor, materials, dedicated project management, taxes, equipment and all other items necessary to complete your project!

It also includes access to your online job portal where you’ll have 24/7 access to your construction schedule, contracts, payment history with remaining balance, change orders, job progress pictures and more.  It’s important, when comparing multiple sources, to make sure you are comparing apples to apples. We will be happy to discuss how we arrived at these figures, so you can make an informed decision.

Complete Kitchen Remodel
Starting at $125,000

“Gut” the old kitchen and in some cases, modify walls and change the kitchen layout.  These projects may include expanding into an adjacent existing space, such as a living room or dining room, to increase the size of the kitchen and connect two common areas.

May move plumbing and appliances

All new cabinetry with solid wood construction, soft-close doors and drawers and built-in heavy duty slide-outs in selected areas

Solid surface countertops like quartz

Solid surface or tile backsplash

New appliances and fixtures

Wood or tile Flooring

New recessed lights 

 Master Bathroom Remodel
Starting at $95,000

“Gut” the old bathroom.

Relocate / reconfigure plumbing locations (shower, tub, toilet, sinks, etc.).

All new cabinetry with solid wood construction, soft-close doors and drawers.

Solid surface countertops like quartz with “his and her” undermount sinks.

New recessed lights with new recessed / fan light combinations installed in water closets, over the tub or in the shower (or all locations). 

Custom mirrors, framed, beveled or oversized in general.

Basement Remodel / Finishing
Starting at $195,000

Remove old finishes as needed (for example: Wood wall panels, drop ceiling systems, flooring, etc.).

If necessary, install water management / drainage system as needed to insure the basement remains dry and clean (no “musty” smells allowed!).

Install new wall framing, insulation and finishes.

Install new air conditioning system.

Install new plumbing fixtures for a bathroom.

Install new wood, tile or luxury vinyl tile flooring.

New recessed lights, plugs and switches.

Porch Remodel or Addition
Starting at $150,000

New covered porch with pressure treated decking installed with hidden fasteners for a clean finish.  

New porch roof will be “tied in” with the existing home’s roof.  

Ceiling may be either open and “airy” with framing exposed or may have a finished tongue and groove ceiling or similar.

Install new or updated single, sliding or oversized bifold doors to connect the new space to the interior of the existing home.

Install ceiling fans, lights, heaters, outdoor rated outlets, speakers or other items as requested.  

Install gas and water lines as needed.

Install individually framed screens to allow for easy repair.

Install wrought iron, powder-coated aluminum, pressure treated or other types of handrails.

All surfaces stained or painted to match or complement the existing home exterior finishes.
